content: 1. Efflux transporters, such as P-glycoprotein (MDR1), play a significant role in drug interactions. Use caution and monitor when co-administering drugs like lumacaftor/ivacaftor or rifampin, as they can affect hepatic enzyme CYP2B6 metabolism. In vitro studies suggest lumacaftor may induce, while ivacaftor may inhibit, CYP2B6 substrates. 2. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of maraviroc by acting on the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of marijuana by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 4. Mavorixafor increases the levels or effects of rifampin via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Use caution and monitor. Co-administration of mavorixafor, a P-gp inhibitor, with sensitive P-gp substrates may lead to serious adverse effects even with minimal substrate concentration changes. 5. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely, as contraceptive failure is possible. 6. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of mefloquine by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 7. Rifampin decreases melatonin levels or effects by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 8. Rifampin reduces mestranol levels or effects via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 9. Rifampin decreases methadone levels by increasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 10. Rifampin reduces methylprednisolone levels or effects via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 11. Rifampin decreases metoprolol levels by increasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 12. Rifampin reduces mexiletine levels or effects by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 13. Rifampin decreases miconazole vaginal levels by increasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 14. Rifampin reduces mifepristone levels or effects by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 15. Co-administration of CYP3A4 inducers with mipomersen has not been studied and is not recommended by the manufacturer. Both drugs may increase hepatic enzyme levels; monitor liver function tests (LFTs). 16. Rifampin decreases mirtazapine levels or effects by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 17. Rifampin increases momelotinib toxicity through mechanisms involving OATP1B1/B3 inhibition, which raises momelotinib plasma concentrations and the risk of adverse reactions. Use caution and monitor. 18. Rifampin reduces montelukast levels or effects by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 19. Nafcillin decreases rifampin effects through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor. Nafcillin may also exhibit antagonistic effects against Staphylococcus aureus. 20. Rifampin decreases nefazodone levels or effects by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 21. Rifampin reduces neomycin PO levels or effects via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 22. Rifampin decreases nifedipine levels or effects by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 23. Rifampin reduces nilotinib levels or effects via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 24. Rifampin decreases nimodipine levels or effects by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 25. Rifampin reduces nitrendipine levels or effects by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 26. Rifampin decreases olanzapine levels or effects by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 27. Rifampin reduces oliceridine levels or effects by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with a CYP3A4 inducer is necessary, consider increasing the oliceridine dose until stable drug effects are achieved. Monitor for signs of opioid withdrawal. If the inducer is discontinued, reduce the oliceridine dosage and monitor for respiratory depression. 28. Rifampin decreases omeprazole levels or effects by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 29. Rifampin reduces ondansetron levels or effects by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 30. Rifampin decreases osilodrostat levels or effects by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Osilodrostat is a substrate of CYP3A4 and CYP2B6. Monitor for signs and symptoms during co-administration and discontinuation with strong CYP3A4 and/or CYP2B6 inducers. 31. Rifampin reduces ospemifene levels by affecting hepatic enzymes CYP3A4, CYP2C19, and CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 32. Rifampin decreases oxybutynin levels or effects by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 33. Rifampin reduces oxycodone levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 34. Rifampin decreases paclitaxel levels or effects by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism, P-glycoprotein efflux transporter, and other mechanisms. Use caution and monitor. Paclitaxel efficacy may decrease when co-administered with CYP2C8 inducers. 35. Rifampin reduces paliperidone levels or effects via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Paliperidone dosage may need to be increased when co-administered with strong inducers of both CYP3A4 and P-gp. 36. Rifampin decreases pantoprazole levels or effects by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 37. Rifampin reduces parecoxib levels or effects by influencing hepatic enzymes CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 38. Rifampin decreases paromomycin levels or effects via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 39. Rifampin reduces pentobarbital levels by increasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 40. Rifampin decreases phenobarbital levels by increasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 41. Rifampin reduces phenytoin levels or effects by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 42. Rifampin decreases pimavanserin levels or effects by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration if possible. Monitor for reduced pimavanserin efficacy, and consider increasing the dosage if necessary. 43. Rifampin reduces pimozide levels or effects by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 44. Rifampin decreases pioglitazone levels or effects by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 45. Rifampin increases pitavastatin levels by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Do not exceed 2 mg/day of pitavastatin. 46. Rifampin reduces pitolisant levels or effects by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Pitolisant exposure decreases by 50% when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inducers. If the inducer is discontinued, reduce the pitolisant dosage by half. 47. Rifampin decreases polatuzumab vedotin levels or effects by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Polatuzumab undergoes catabolism to small peptides, amino acids, monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE), and unconjugated MMAE-related catabolites. MMAE is a CYP3A4 substrate. Co-administration with a strong CYP3A4 inducer may decrease unconjugated MMAE AUC. 48. Ponatinib increases rifampin levels via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 49. Rifampin reduces posaconazole levels or effects by influencing the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter and increasing metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 50. Rifampin increases pravastatin toxicity through mechanisms involving OATP1B1 inhibition, which may increase the risk of myopathy. Use caution and monitor. 51. Rifampin decreases prednisolone levels or effects via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 52. Rifampin reduces prednisone levels or effects via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 53. Pretomanid increases rifampin levels or effects through unspecified mechanisms. Use caution and monitor. Increased monitoring for drug-related adverse effects is recommended if pretomanid is co-administered with sensitive OATP1B3 substrates. 54. Rifampin decreases primidone levels by increasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 55. Pyrazinamide reduces probenecid effects through an unknown mechanism. Probenecid increases rifampin levels or effects through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Concomitant use with probenecid increases rifampin concentrations, which may elevate the risk of toxicity. Monitor for adverse reactions during co-administration. 56. Rifampin reduces propafenone levels or effects by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and increasing metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 57. Pyrazinamide and valoctocogene roxaparvovec both increase hepatotoxicity risk through additive effects. Use caution and monitor. Medications that may cause hepatotoxicity when combined with valoctocogene roxaparvovec may potentiate the risk of elevated liver enzymes. Monitor these medications closely and consider alternatives in case of potential drug interactions. 58. Rifampin decreases acetaminophen levels by increasing its metabolism. Enhanced metabolism may increase levels of hepatotoxic metabolites. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 59. Rifampin reduces acetaminophen IV and rectal levels by increasing metabolism. Enhanced metabolism may increase hepatotoxic metabolite levels. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 60. Rifampin decreases aliskiren levels or effects via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 61. Rifampin reduces alosetron levels or effects by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 62. Rifampin decreases alvimopan levels or effects via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 63. Rifampin reduces ampicillin levels by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 64. Bentonite decreases rifampin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 65. Rifampin decreases bisoprolol levels by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 66. Rifampin reduces caffeine levels or effects by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 67. Rifampin decreases celecoxib levels or effects by influencing hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 68. Rifampin reduces chloramphenicol levels by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 69. Rifampin decreases chlordiazepoxide levels by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 70. Rifampin reduces cimetidine levels or effects by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 71. Clofazimine decreases rifampin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 72. Rifampin reduces diazepam levels or effects by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 73. Rifampin decreases diclofenac levels or effects by influencing hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 74. Rifampin reduces enalapril levels by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 75. Ethanol decreases rifampin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents and is more likely with chronic ethanol use. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 76. Rifampin reduces fexofenadine levels or effects via the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 77. Fluconazole decreases rifampin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 78. Rifampin reduces flurbiprofen levels or effects by influencing hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 79. Rifampin decreases fluvastatin levels by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism and increasing metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 80. Rifampin reduces fosinopril levels by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 81. Rifampin decreases frovatriptan levels or effects by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 82. Rifampin reduces ibuprofen levels or effects by influencing hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 83. Rifampin decreases ibuprofen IV levels by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 84. Rifampin reduces imidapril levels by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 85. Isoniazid and pyrazinamide increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, leading to additive hepatotoxicity. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 86. Rifampin decreases isosorbide dinitrate levels or effects by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown.
